questions.text: What is the central idea of the passage?
options: Sleeping replaces the need for regular study.
Sleep supports learning and should be part of a healthy routine.
Screen exposure has no relationship with sleep.
Memory develops only during the daytime.

passage.text: Sleep is an important biological process that supports learning and memory. During sleep, the brain processes information acquired during the day and helps consolidate some of it into long-term memory. Insufficient sleep can interfere with attention, decision-making and the ability to recall information accurately. A regular sleep schedule may support better sleep quality, while excessive screen exposure immediately before bedtime can make it harder for some people to fall asleep. Good sleep habits should therefore be regarded as part of a healthy learning routine, rather than as time taken away from study.

questions.explanation: The passage links sleep to learning and a healthy routine.
